H001: Implement Keystone Operator packaging **Size:** 🔨 medium **Category:** infrastructure **Priority:** high ## Open Questions All questions resolved by user decisions. No remaining ambiguities. ## Summary Create the packaging layer for the Keystone operator: a multi-stage Dockerfile (Go 1.25 builder → distroless runtime), a Helm chart with all deployment manifests (Deployment, Service, ServiceAccount, RBAC, webhook configs, CRDs), and a FluxCD HelmRelease to deploy it via GitOps. This connects the existing operator code (`operators/keystone/`) to the existing FluxCD deployment pipeline (`deploy/flux-system/`), completing Phase 8 (S017) of the project plan. ## Scope **Included:** - `operators/keystone/Dockerfile` — multi-stage build (golang:1.25 builder, gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot runtime, CGO_ENABLED=0, UID 65532). Build context must be workspace root to resolve `go.work` and `internal/common` dependency. - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/Chart.yaml` — apiVersion v2, chart metadata - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/values.yaml` — image, replicas (default 2), resources, leaderElection (default true), webhook, metrics, serviceAccount - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/crds/keystone.openstack.c5c3.io_keystones.yaml` — CRD copied from `config/crd/bases/` - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/deployment.yaml` - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/service.yaml` - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/serviceaccount.yaml` - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/clusterrole.yaml` - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/clusterrolebinding.yaml` - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/webhook-configuration.yaml` (both MutatingWebhookConfiguration and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration) - `operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/templates/_helpers.tpl` - `deploy/flux-system/releases/keystone-operator.yaml` — FluxCD HelmRelease targeting `openstack` namespace - Update `deploy/flux-system/kustomization.yaml` to include the new HelmRelease resource **Excluded:** - CI/CD workflows for building/pushing operator image or Helm chart (S018 — separate feature) - Makefile `docker-build` and `helm-package` target implementations (separate feature per PLAN.md) - `values-prod.yaml` or environment-specific overrides (YAGNI) - `NOTES.txt` post-install template (YAGNI) - Helm chart tests (YAGNI for initial packaging) - HelmRepository source for c5c3-charts (`deploy/flux-system/sources/c5c3-charts.yaml` already exists) - Monitoring/alerting resources — PrometheusRule, ServiceMonitor (separate concern) - New namespace manifest (`openstack` already exists in `namespaces.yaml`) ## Visualization ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph build ["Dockerfile - Multi-stage Build"] B1["golang:1.25 builder"] B2["CGO_ENABLED=0 go build"] B3["distroless/static:nonroot"] B1 --> B2 --> B3 end subgraph helm ["Helm Chart - mariadb-operator, memcached-operator HR->>H: Install/Upgrade chart H->>K: Apply CRDs from crds/ H->>K: Create ServiceAccount H->>K: Create ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding H->>K: Create Deployment (2 replicas) H->>K: Create Service (webhook 443 to 9443, metrics 8080) H->>K: Create MutatingWebhookConfiguration H->>K: Create ValidatingWebhookConfiguration K->>CM: cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from annotation CM-->>K: Inject CA bundle into webhook configs K-->>H: Resources ready H-->>HR: Release healthy HR-->>FC: Ready=True ``` ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph deps ["HelmRelease Dependency Chain"] CM["cert-manager"] MDB["mariadb-operator"] MC["memcached-operator"] ES["external-secrets"] KS["keystone-operator"] CM --> MDB CM --> MC CM --> ES MDB --> KS MC --> KS CM --> KS end ``` ## Key Components - **`operators/keystone/Dockerfile`**: Two-stage build. Builder stage uses `golang:1.25`, copies `go.work`, `go.sum`, and all three module directories (`internal/common/`, `operators/keystone/`, `operators/c5c3/`) for workspace-aware dependency resolution. Builds with `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -a -o manager ./operators/keystone/main.go`. Runtime stage copies binary to `gcr.io/distroless/static:nonroot`, runs as UID 65532:65532. Docker build context is workspace root (`/workspace`), not `operators/keystone/`. - **`Chart.yaml`**: Chart name `keystone-operator`, apiVersion `v2`, type `application`, version `0.1.0`, appVersion `0.1.0`. - **`values.yaml`**: Configurable image (repo/tag/pullPolicy), replicas (default 2), resource requests/limits, leaderElection toggle (default true), webhook enable/disable, metrics port (default 8080 — matches bootstrap default `--metrics-bind-address :8080`), serviceAccount name/create flag. - **`crds/keystone.openstack.c5c3.io_keystones.yaml`**: Copy of generated CRD from `config/crd/bases/`. Helm auto-installs CRDs from `crds/` directory before templates. - **`templates/deployment.yaml`**: Operator Deployment using `bootstrap.Run()` flags: `--leader-elect={{ .Values.leaderElection.enabled }}`, `--metrics-bind-address=:{{ .Values.metrics.port }}`, `--health-probe-bind-address=:8081`. Liveness/readiness probes on `:8081` (`/healthz`, `/readyz`). Security context: non-root, read-only rootfs, drop ALL capabilities, `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, `runAsNonRoot: true`. Resource limits from values. Webhook port 9443 exposed on container. - **`templates/service.yaml`**: ClusterIP service exposing webhook port (443→9443) and metrics port (8080). - **`templates/serviceaccount.yaml`**: Conditionally created SA via `{{ if .Values.serviceAccount.create }}`. - **`templates/clusterrole.yaml`**: RBAC rules derived from `+kubebuilder:rbac` markers in `keystone_controller.go`: - `keystone.openstack.c5c3.io`: keystones, keystones/status, keystones/finalizers - `apps`: deployments - `""` (core): services, configmaps, secrets, serviceaccounts, events - `batch`: jobs, cronjobs - `k8s.mariadb.com`: databases, users, grants - `external-secrets.io`: externalsecrets, pushsecrets - `rbac.authorization.k8s.io`: roles, rolebindings - **`templates/clusterrolebinding.yaml`**: Binds ClusterRole to the operator's ServiceAccount in the `openstack` namespace. - **`templates/webhook-configuration.yaml`**: Both `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` (defaulting, path `/mutate-keystone-openstack-c5c3-io-v1alpha1-keystone`, operations: CREATE+UPDATE, name: `mkeystone.kb.io`) and `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` (validation, path `/validate-keystone-openstack-c5c3-io-v1alpha1-keystone`, operations: CREATE+UPDATE+DELETE, name: `vkeystone.kb.io`). Both with `failurePolicy: Fail`, `sideEffects: None`, and `cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from` annotation for automatic CA bundle injection. - **`templates/_helpers.tpl`**: Standard helpers — `fullname`, `name`, `chart`, `labels`, `selectorLabels`, `serviceAccountName`. - **`deploy/flux-system/releases/keystone-operator.yaml`**: HelmRelease (apiVersion `helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2`) targeting `openstack` namespace. References `c5c3-charts` OCI HelmRepository (namespace `flux-system`). `dependsOn: [cert-manager, mariadb-operator, memcached-operator]` with correct namespace references. `install.crds: CreateReplace`, `upgrade.crds: CreateReplace`, `remediation.retries: 3`. Version range `>=0.1.0 <1.0.0`. Interval `30m`. Values override: `replicas: 2`, `leaderElection.enabled: true`. - **`deploy/flux-system/kustomization.yaml`**: Add `releases/keystone-operator.yaml` to the resources list (alongside existing Verify all rendered YAML is valid, all resources have correct labels, security contexts, RBAC rules match kubebuilder markers, probe endpoints match bootstrap.Run() defaults, webhook paths match config/webhook/manifests.yaml (CC-0017, REQ-001 through REQ-010) 5.2 Create reference documentation at docs/reference/backend/keystone-operator-packaging.md covering: Dockerfile build instructions (build context, build args, image layers), Helm chart configuration reference (all values.yaml parameters with types, defaults, and descriptions), FluxCD HelmRelease configuration, dependency chain diagram, and CRD installation behavior (CC-0017) Architecture: This is a pure infrastructure packaging feature — no application code changes. All files are declarative YAML/Dockerfile with no business logic. Dockerfile Strategy: Multi-stage build with workspace root context. The Go workspace (go.work) with replace directives requires all modules (internal/common/, operators/keystone/, operators/c5c3/) to be available at build time. Build stage copies go.work, go.sum files first for layer caching, then copies source directories. Runtime stage is distroless/static:nonroot for minimal attack surface. Helm Chart Design: Standard kubebuilder-style operator chart. values.yaml exposes operational knobs without exposing template complexity. _helpers.tpl follows Helm best practices with standard label/selector helpers. CRD is in crds/ directory (not templates/) so Helm installs it before templates, avoiding chicken-and-egg issues. RBAC Derivation: ClusterRole rules are manually derived from kubebuilder RBAC markers in keystone_controller.go. This is a one-time manual step since we don't have make manifests generating the Helm chart. Future CI should validate RBAC rules match markers. Webhook Configuration: Both MutatingWebhookConfiguration and ValidatingWebhookConfiguration reference the operator Service for webhook callbacks. cert-manager.io/inject-ca-from annotation enables automatic CA bundle injection from cert-manager Certificate resource. Webhook port is 9443 (container) mapped to 443 (Service). FluxCD Integration: HelmRelease follows the established pattern (memcached-operator.yaml as reference). dependsOn ensures cert-manager (for TLS), mariadb-operator (for Database/User/Grant CRDs), and memcached-operator (for Memcached CRDs) are ready before keystone-operator starts. Key Pitfalls: 1. Build context must be workspace root, not operators/keystone/ — the go.work replace directive breaks otherwise 2. RBAC rules must exactly match kubebuilder markers — events only gets create;patch, external-secrets resources don't get delete 3. Webhook service name in configurations must match the Service created by the chart 4. Health probe port 8081 is hardcoded in bootstrap.Run() defaults — not configurable via values 5.
